title: PostHog token-scrub pinned only by substring presence — a regex regression that disables redaction keeps both pinned substrings and stays green
detail: The scrub keeps the 288-bit continue token out of the analytics store, but the test asserts only two substrings of the inline JS; the replacement string and character class — the parts that actually redact — are unpinned, and the regex can't execute inside a Gleam test.
recommended_fix: Pin the full sanitize_properties function body verbatim (one string.contains over the whole snippet fragment), or move the scrub into a static JS asset and cover the regex behavior in scripts/js-tests.

title: Advisory test gate: PASS
detail: Chunk-3 traceability (the feature's test suite): P0 100% — save/continue-link/resume/erasure endpoints (happy + 400/closed/uniform-404/cooldown/replay), the r3 no-oracle pin (no "sent" in body), strip via real handle_post_form, tombstone no-resurrect, expiry sweep + RunSummary count, cascade, CSRF/public-path/redact/body-size arms with true boundaries (9-vs-11 min, 64 KB ±1, 500-vs-501, 3-vs-4). P1 ~95% — filter_fields, all 8 SQL queries, resume-page render + backdated timing, email builders both variants; sole partials: scrub regex semantics (finding above) and per-route CL/TE matrix sampling. Overall ~96% >= 80%.
recommended_fix: Gate passes; no action required. Verbatim-pinning the scrub snippet (finding above) would close the one weak assertion.
